title: The Runner Who Won Olympic Gold In A Car
sources: Wikipedia, 'Frederick Lorz': dropped out at 9 miles, his manager drove him ~11 miles, the car broke down, he ran the last stretch, broke the tape, was cheered as winner (Alice Roosevelt photo) until confronted, claimed it was a joke; AAU banned him for life, commuted to 6 months in Feb 1905; he legitimately won the 1905 Boston Marathon (2:38:25)

Wikipedia, 'Thomas Hicks (athlete)' and 'Athletics at the 1904 Summer Olympics - Men's marathon': Hicks won in 3:28:53, the slowest Olympic marathon time, aided by strychnine sulfate + egg white + brandy (multiple doses), hallucinating and near collapse, carried by trainers over much of the final stretch per the 1905 Lucas and Spalding reports

Smithsonian Magazine, 'How the 1904 Marathon Became One of the Weirdest Olympic Events of All Time': ~90F heat, dirt roads, cars raising dust, water only at a tower at ~6 miles and a well at ~10, doctors deferred water to study 'purposeful dehydration', strychnine is used primarily as a pesticide to kill rats (CDC), William Garcia nearly died from dust-afflicted stomach hemorrhaging

Olympics.com, 'The strange case of the St Louis 1904 marathon': Len Taunyane chased about a mile off course by wild dogs, finished 9th; Felix Carvajal laid low by stomach cramps after eating apples, finished 4th; strychnine in high doses is rat poison
Runner's World, 'The Unbelievable True Story of the 1904 Olympic Marathon': only 14 of 32 starters finished; Carvajal the Cuban postman; first recorded case of Olympic doping

lines.text: by riding the marathon in a car.
lines.caps: by | RIDING THE MARATHON | in a CAR.

lines.text: See, at the nineteen oh four Olympics, athletes ran the marathon on a dirt road in brutal heat,
lines.caps: SEE, | AT THE | 1904 OLYMPICS, | athletes ran | the MARATHON | on a | DIRT ROAD | in BRUTAL HEAT,

lines.text: and the race director refused to give them water,
lines.caps: the RACE DIRECTOR | refused | to give | RUNNERS WATER,

lines.text: so he could study what dehydration does to the body.
lines.caps: so he could | STUDY | what DEHYDRATION DOES | to the BODY.

lines.text: Cars kicked up clouds of dust. Runners cramped, collapsed, and quit.
lines.caps: CARS kicked up | CLOUDS of dust. | RUNNERS CRAMPED, | collapsed, | and QUIT.

lines.text: One Cuban postman stopped mid-race to snack on rotten apples.
lines.caps: one CUBAN POSTMAN | stopped mid-race | to snack on | ROTTEN APPLES.

lines.text: And a South African runner got chased a mile off course by a pack of wild dogs.
lines.caps: a South | African RUNNER | got CHASED | a mile off course | by WILD DOGS.

lines.text: Meanwhile, the leader, Thomas Hicks, was begging for water.
lines.caps: the LEADER, | THOMAS HICKS, | was BEGGING | for WATER.

lines.text: So his trainers gave him something better.
lines.caps: so his TRAINERS | gave him | something BETTER.

lines.text: Strychnine, rat poison, mixed with raw egg white and brandy.
lines.caps: STRYCHNINE, | RAT POISON, | mixed with | RAW EGG WHITE | and BRANDY.

lines.text: He hallucinated, collapsed at the finish, and was carried over the line.
lines.caps: he HALLUCINATED, | COLLAPSED | at the finish, | CARRIED | over the LINE.

lines.text: He still won gold, in three hours, twenty eight minutes,
lines.caps: he STILL | won GOLD, | in 3 HOURS, | 28 MINUTES,

lines.text: still the slowest winning time in Olympic history.
lines.caps: still the | SLOWEST winning time | in OLYMPIC HISTORY.

lines.text: Oh, and Fred Lorz? He said it was just a joke.
lines.caps: oh, and | FRED LORZ? | he said it was | JUST A JOKE.

lines.text: A year later, un-banned, he won the Boston Marathon, for real.
lines.caps: a YEAR LATER, | UN-BANNED, | he won | the BOSTON MARATHON, | for REAL.
